issues.legal_issue: A will that makes its dispositive scheme depend on appendices is incomplete when those appendices did not exist at execution and cannot be incorporated or used to complete the will.
material_facts: The will referred to appendices to identify the specific property and beneficiaries and to set out how the property was to be distributed.
The appendices were not in existence when the will was executed, were not signed by the attesting witnesses, and were not proved to have formed part of the executed instrument.
Without the appendices, the will did not specify the distributions needed to implement the testatrix’s stated intentions.
issues.conclusion: The appendices could not be incorporated into the will, and the will could not be given effect without them; probate of that will was therefore refused. Sections 87 and 103 did not cure the defect.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 64 of the Indian Succession Act, a document incorporated by reference must be identifiable and already in existence when the will is executed, and the testator must know its contents. This principle is supported by Sarabjit Rick Singh v. Union of India and Singleton v. Tomlinson. Section 87 does not permit an incomplete will to be completed or an intention absent from the executed instrument to be supplied; the will must be construed as a whole, and severance is available only for a severable part, as discussed in Bajrang Factory Ltd. v. University of Calcutta. Section 103, concerning residuary bequests, did not apply to these facts.

predicates.probate_application: A party asks a court to grant probate or administration on the basis of a testamentary instrument.
predicates.will_makes_distributions_depend_on_appen: The will relies on appendices to specify or implement its property distributions.
predicates.appendices_not_existing_at_execution: The referenced appendices did not exist when the testator executed the will.
predicates.appendices_not_proved_as_part_of_execute: The appendices were not authenticated or otherwise proved to have formed part of the instrument as executed.

issues.definition: When a probate application relies on a will whose distributions depend on appendices that did not exist at execution and are not proved to be part of the executed will, the will is treated as incomplete and probate is refused.

issues.legal_issue: Formal proof of a will is insufficient to establish its genuineness when suspicious circumstances exist and the propounder does not satisfactorily remove them.
material_facts: The testatrix was elderly, and the appellant took an active part in preparing and executing the will.
The will remained in the appellant’s custody, and the appellant did not disclose it to close relatives for a considerable time.
One attesting witness was not examined, and neither attesting witness signed the appendices on which the distributions depended.
The evidence showed that the appendices were not part of the will when it was executed, and the court found the will surrounded by suspicious circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The propounder did not establish the will as genuine to the court’s satisfaction, and the refusal to grant probate was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 63(c) of the Indian Succession Act and 68 of the Indian Evidence Act require proof of execution through an attesting witness where one is available and capable of giving evidence; attestation requires an intention to attest. The propounder bears the burden of proving valid execution, the testator’s free and informed act, and a sound disposing mind, and must remove any suspicious circumstances with sufficient evidence. Formal compliance alone is not enough, and the probate court must satisfy its conscience because its grant is a judgment in rem. The Court relied on B. Venkatamuni v. C.J. Ayodhya Ram Singh, Niranjan Umeshchandra Joshi v. Mrudula Jyoti Rao, Adivekka v. Hanamavva, Benga Behera v. Braja Kishore Nanda, Madhukar D. Shende v. Tarabai Shedage, Sridevi v. Jayaraja Shetty, and Savithri v. Karthyayani Amma; deprivation of an heir’s share alone is not necessarily suspicious, but the surrounding facts must be considered rationally.

predicates.probate_application: A party asks a court to grant probate or administration on the basis of a testamentary instrument.
predicates.will_surrounded_by_suspicious_circumstan: The circumstances surrounding preparation, custody, disclosure, execution, or supporting material give reason to doubt that the will is the testator’s genuine act.
predicates.propounder_fails_to_remove_suspicion: The person seeking probate does not provide sufficient and cogent evidence to satisfy the court that the suspicious circumstances are resolved.

issues.definition: If a probate application concerns a will surrounded by suspicious circumstances that the propounder does not remove with sufficient evidence, probate is refused because genuineness has not been established.
